target_name: Tail-compressed cover of capex and maturing debt
rationale: This is the archive's gen-4 "Same-period cover of capex and maturing debt" with the winsorization parameter changed from 1% to 10% — the textbook definition of a cosmetic variant, and the stated concavity hypothesis could be tested far more informatively with a genuine transform (log, rank, or capped-at-1 coverage) than by re-running the same expression at a different trim.

The MIN is likely degenerate — gross profit almost always exceeds cash earnings net of working-capital change for the typical firm, so the operator will select the cash-generation leg in the large majority of firm-years and the signal will collapse into a near-duplicate of the existing t=5.71 archive signal; the "prudence rule" only bites if the two legs are comparably scaled, which they are not.

target_name: Proportional coverage plus absolute spare capacity
rationale: Both legs share the identical numerator quantity (cash generation less capex and current debt) and differ only in scaling denominator, so this is a rank-space reweighting of two already-tested, mechanically correlated versions of the same construct rather than a new economic statement — and the proposal's own defense concedes a prior rank blend was already rejected on these grounds.

The two legs are genuinely distinct economic channels (financing adequacy versus realized output response) and the depreciation floor is a defensible fix to the diagnosed 1/capex explosion, but be aware the output leg has now twice produced a *negatively* signed FMB slope, so a rank blend risks diluting the cross-sectional evidence the objective prizes — report leg-level slopes alongside the composite.

target_name: Commitment escalation per dollar of revenue
rationale: DELTA(capx)/sale is essentially the published abnormal-capital-investment/investment-growth anomaly and DELTA(dlc)/sale is the short-term component of the net-external-financing anomaly, so summing them is a mashup of two well-documented effects, and the sum is dimensionally awkward (a change in an annual expenditure flow added to a change in a balance-sheet stock) with no argument for equal weighting.

target_name: Worst-year surplus per dollar of assets
rationale: Applying TS_MIN to the asset-scaled surplus rather than the coverage ratio is a substantive normalization change with a clearly articulated diagnosis of why both prior durability attempts underperformed, though the result will be strongly correlated with the level of the asset-scaled surplus (fmb 3.54, alpha 4.3%) and may be driven by a stale worst year, so the incremental information over that leg should be verified directly.
